topic: Apple Music drops its red icon

slides.title: Apple Music just dropped its red
slides.sub: A new beta swaps the red and pink icon for black and white, and plenty of people hate it. Here's the branding lesson for your business.

slides.title: What changed
slides.body: In iOS 27.2 beta 4, the Apple Music icon turned black and white. Widgets went black, and red accents inside the app switched to blue.

slides.title: Why people pushed back
slides.body: Many commenters called the new icon boring and generic. Apple hasn't confirmed a full rebrand, and beta designs can still change.

slides.title: Big brands can drop color
slides.body: A giant brand has the name, the reach and years of memory to carry it. A growing business usually needs its color to do that work.

slides.title: Test your logo in one color
slides.body: Put your logo in plain black, then plain white. If it still reads as you, your mark is strong. If it falls apart, it leans too hard on color.

slides.title: Pick a color and own it
slides.body: Choose one main brand color and use it the same way on your sign, site, socials and packaging, so people know you before they read your name.

slides.title: Build a brand people know in any color
slides.body: We design logos, color systems and full brand identities for Black-owned businesses, built to work in full color and in plain black and white.

caption:
Apple Music logo change checklist: 4 brand color checks for Black-owned businesses after Apple dropped its red icon.

On October 13, Apple released iOS 27.2 beta 4, and the Apple Music icon changed from its familiar red and pink to black and white. Widgets now use black backgrounds, and red accents inside the app switched to blue. Many people online called the new icon boring and generic. Apple hasn't formally announced a full rebrand, and beta designs can still change before iOS 27.2's public release, expected later in October.

Here's what to check on your own brand:
1. Your logo still reads in plain black and in plain white.
2. You have one main brand color, written down with its exact color codes.
3. That color shows up the same way on your sign, site, socials and packaging.
4. Your logo is still clear at profile-picture size.

Apple has the reach to ride out a color change. Most growing businesses need their color working for them every single day.

caption_drafts.explainer:
Apple Music's new black-and-white icon has people talking, and it holds a real lesson for small business branding.

In iOS 27.2 beta 4, released October 13, Apple replaced the red and pink Apple Music icon with a black-and-white one that flips for dark mode. Widgets went black and in-app accents moved from red to blue. Reactions online were mostly negative, with many calling it boring and generic. Apple hasn't confirmed a full rebrand, and betas can still change.

A company that size can lean on its name and reach. A growing Black-owned business usually leans on its color and logo to be remembered, so those need to be strong and consistent.

On October 13, iOS 27.2 beta 4 swapped the red and pink Apple Music icon for black and white. Widgets went black and red accents turned blue. Many people called it boring and generic. Apple hasn't confirmed a full rebrand, and the beta can still change.

Apple can survive a bland icon on the strength of its name. A neighborhood bakery or a new skincare line usually can't. When your color and logo are doing the recognizing, they have to be distinct and used the same way everywhere.
